findings.title: Successful PL input evaluations lack a saved actual scheduling witness
findings.sha_unavailable_reason: Concurrent repair preceded the first file hash; the old source was read through the tool before repair.
evidence: The original kernel retained interval_index/substep_index/substep_count/stage only in the current/stages local records and attached those records on exceptions.
The original successful return was return {"path": np.stack(output), "rk4_updates": updates}.

The paths wrapper dispatched input_eval with no scheduling details; the journal defaulted details to null. Successful records therefore contained input_eval indices/counts without each actual interval/stage/fraction.
findings.trigger: Any successful historical PL rollout, even with every numerical and physical gate passing.
findings.impact: The independent new-run-only audit cannot verify the actual four-stage PL input schedule required by protocol section 4. Reconstructing an intended schedule from source and input nodes is not a saved witness of the calls that occurred.
findings.repair_direction: Record interval, substep, count, stage, numerator/fraction and actual returned/used input at the existing callback invocation, either in journal details or a compact returned witness. Preserve only genuinely attempted/returned entries on failure. Do not add input evaluations or RHS calls.
findings.required_regression: A successful nonconstant PL case and injected input callback failures must preserve exactly the actual schedule prefix, endpoint identity, four stage fractions, and unchanged scientific operation counts.
findings.coordinator_response: Repair in progress: compact schedule witness added after this observation; separate exact v2 review and regression still required.

findings.title: Measured short writes can remain successful and be sealed
findings.sha_unavailable_reason: Concurrent repair preceded the first file hash; do not substitute an earlier engineering receipt SHA for the actual text read.
evidence: The original measured write counted returned bytes, incremented short_writes when actual < requested, then returned without poisoning or raising.
write_json delegates chunks to json.dump without checking each stream.write return; archive writers likewise rely on stream write semantics.
The seal precondition checked poisoned/unknown/active handles but did not reject short_writes. Hashing the resulting bytes alone cannot prove that the intended evidence was fully written.
findings.trigger: An underlying evidence writer returns a known count smaller than the request without raising; a JSON chunk or NPZ segment is truncated.
findings.impact: A damaged result record can be closed and hashed as successful, losing evidence or altering a saved scalar despite normal scientific counters.
findings.repair_direction: Reject any invalid or short write count immediately as a global persistence failure. Retain the known returned byte count and the short-write flag; do not relabel a known short return as an unknown prefix. Normal short reads at EOF remain valid when the caller's length/hash check permits them.
findings.required_regression: Inject a known short write through the actual evidence writer and assert permanent poison, no successful scope/seal, retained requested/returned counts, and zero unknown-byte increments for that known return.
findings.coordinator_response: Repair in progress: stop-on-short-write added after this observation; separate exact v2 review and regression still required.

findings.title: Failures during the unmetered sealing tail lose actual I/O progress
evidence: seal_result runs after OutputIO exits, maintaining manifest/hash_bytes and file read/write state only as local variables.

The successful tail return reports total reads/writes, but the original function has no failure ledger or exception partial attachment for hash reads, source-line counting, summary writes/fsync, manifest writes/fsync, or the final manifest hash.

The outer fatal_prefix saves io.snapshot from before sealing, so a sealing exception does not preserve the sealing actions already attempted or returned. The exact checks on the two final write_tail calls do not by themselves close this gap.
findings.trigger: Any sealing hash read, summary/manifest write, flush, fsync, close or final hash fails after one or more earlier tail operations returned.
findings.impact: The campaign stops, but its I/O accounting and failure evidence omit the actual finite tail prefix. A reviewer cannot reconcile attempted/returned/failed sealing actions or known versus unknown byte returns.
findings.repair_direction: Use a finite append-only tail ledger or equivalent exception-attached progress record with action identity, attempted/returned/failed status, actual returned bytes, and durability outcome. Preserve the original error and serialize the tail partial through the independent fatal evidence writer. Continue to forbid resealing/retry and adjust the I/O envelope if new actions are introduced.
findings.required_regression: Inject failures after at least one successful tail hash, during source-line reading, summary write/fsync, manifest write/fsync and final hash. Confirm complete known prefixes, explicit unknown interrupted operations, no invented returns, no successful final seal, and no scientific recomputation.
findings.coordinator_response: Repair in progress: coordinator is implementing a bounded TailLedger; not reviewed in this v1.

verified_control_properties.dependency_field: ScopeStore now reads prerequisite_scope_ids; earlier field mismatch is resolved in the observed controller.
verified_control_properties.count_semantics: Nested callback/process categories are not disjoint scalar scientific primitives.
verified_control_properties.phase_freezes: Controller saves all original history/reset or future records, JSON/NPZ hashes, the closed-scope count/end offset/closure-chain digest, then reader.advance binds the freeze SHA before the next phase is loaded.
verified_control_properties.failure_population: Numerical failures consume scopes; all_success dependants remain explicit zero-work failures; group/pair summaries retain original weights and missing mass. No retry or complete-case replacement is introduced by the inspected control flow.
verified_control_properties.physical_input_flow: Single rhs=btilde4+weighted_impulse(point) solve using saved factors; historical inputs use all eleven recorded point columns; each step keeps its own latent history endpoint, resets visible q/v and saves reset energies; future uses original constant_power with the actual delta_u retained.
verified_control_properties.source_and_parameter_flow: Whitelisted reader phases and source metadata proof precede model construction. I/E/truth decode follows the future freeze. E ancestry uses nine bounded in-memory hashes. Parameters are compared against saved arrays before and after the campaign; final parameter scope is last.
verified_control_properties.metric_boundary: All six seed/step comparisons are independently required for each I/E reference; V=false forces both group gates false. No labels, LOS or new missed-instability claim is introduced.
